analysis:
Examined both ClusterService.swift excerpts, ClusterServiceControl.swift metadata and its complete supplied patch against the indexed model and detailed T-041. The Service excerpts at head 911–1577 are unchanged according to the complete range map: they cover prompt collection, status/cache reporting, worker-digest update replanning, approval synchronization, process supervision, draining and log handling. They do not establish a new encryption, account-cache isolation, authorization or billing regression; underlying serving/cache implementations were not supplied. Approval fallback and listener binding in these unchanged excerpts must not be reported as newly introduced defects.
The control patch at head 109–119 replaces cable-only checks and context selection with listenerChange/listenerSelection and supplies listening.controlPort and listening.policy to the responder. Head 176–182 additionally invalidates control state when the local member identity changes, improving re-pairing isolation rather than visibly weakening it. No supported finding follows from these calls alone.
Integration must examine the changed ClusterService.swift composition at head 164–175 and listener lifecycle code at 337–420, together with Listening, listenerChange, listenerSelection and Responder policy enforcement: confirm public defaults retain cable-restricted authenticated pairing, old listeners/connections lose authority after key or peer changes, and configurable policy does not unintentionally widen network reachability. These contracts are outside this batch, not observed missing controls. Relevant concerns are A-001/A-018, TB-002/TB-003/TB-007 and authorization freshness under T-053; cluster pairing's relationship to canonical endpoint authorization also needs reconciliation using the other source passes. No claim of deployment or full qualification is made.
